nodes.description: ROBO4 is expressed in the endocardium of the developing outflow-tract cushions and later in endothelial and interstitial cells of the developing aortic valve. Robo4-deficient mice develop valve thickening, bicuspid and occasionally quadricuspid valves, and valve stenosis or regurgitation. Valve pathology from an affected family member with BAV showed valve thickening with a fibroproliferative process.

nodes.description: ROBO4-deficient aortic endothelial cells express alpha-smooth muscle actin and SNAI1, elongate and invade collagen gels, a pattern the authors read as suggestive of endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition. In the patient's aneurysm, ROBO4-positive cells co-staining for alpha-smooth muscle actin were found in the aortic media. No single signaling pathway was identified: ROBO4 silencing gave a modest decline in BMP and Notch target-gene expression without altered TGF-beta responses.

nodes.description: Heterozygous germline ROBO4 variants reduce or structurally disrupt the endothelial ROBO4 receptor. The family 1 splice-donor variant causes in-frame skipping of exon 13, removing 36 amino acids from the intracellular domain; the family 2 missense variant p.Arg64Cys changes a conserved residue in the first extracellular Ig-like domain. Silencing and mutant-expression experiments point to loss of function, by haploinsufficiency or an antimorphic effect of mutant protein, as the pathogenic mechanism.
